gemma4-26b-a4b-gpu on apple-m5-max — 2026-10-22

Generated by python3 -m aeb.report from 12 headline benchmark processes plus 84 input-length sweep processes. Raw per-request data: data.json. Methodology: benchmark_methodology.md.

Gemma 4 26B A4B (MoE, 3.8B active) on the Apple M5 Max GPU, run natively on macOS with Metal: LiteRT-LM (ML Drift GPU backend), llama.cpp (Metal), MLX (mlx-lm) and BaseRT. Every configuration is a reference (open) comparison: each framework runs its own published ~4-bit artifact of the model with framework defaults, so weights and quantization are NOT matched and speed must be read together with the accuracy gate. Native macOS numbers are not comparable with the Linux-VM CPU suites.

Results

Throughput

Input-length throughput sweep

Sweep measurement dates (UTC): 2026-10-22.

Fixed 512 generated tokens, greedy with stop tokens ignored; common context capacity 16,896. Model artifacts and thread counts are unchanged from the configurations above. These are reference configurations, not matched weights. The original headline workload remains unchanged.

Each point uses 3 interleaved processes per configuration, 2 warm-ups and 5 measured requests per process. Long inputs repeat the same public-domain passage deterministically. N includes BOS and chat-template tokens. Each request starts with an empty KV cache.

Prefill tokens/s = N / time to first token (includes tokenization and first-token generation). Decode tokens/s = 511 / time from the first to the last generated token. Rates are medians; brackets show min-max. Failed, truncated or wrong-length processes are excluded, never replaced by estimated rates.

Publicly reported accuracy

Google publishes no original-MMLU or GSM8K score for Gemma 4 26B A4B; the model card (revision 4d7ae4984b7d) reports MMLU-Pro, MMMLU, GPQA Diamond, AIME 2026, LiveCodeBench v6 and BigBench Extra Hard for the instruction-tuned bf16 model, and labels only the Gemma 3 27B comparison column 'no think'. None of these setups matches this harness (zero-shot, thinking disabled, greedy, ~4-bit weights, answer-prefilled MMLU, 512-token GSM8K cap), so they are context, not a pass/fail threshold; the frameworks are judged against each other on identical items.

  • Order-of-magnitude check: the same table puts 26B A4B 22.6 points above E2B on MMLU Pro. This harness measured 57-61% MMLU and 76-78% GSM8K for E2B on the identical subsets (2026-10-02 CPU report), so a healthy 26B A4B configuration should score clearly higher on both.
  • The 26B A4B chat template closes a non-thinking model turn with an empty thought channel ('<|channel>thought\n<channel|>'); the model card states that all Gemma 4 models except E2B/E4B emit this empty block when thinking is disabled. This suite's prompts include it (workload.chat_template = gemma4-empty-thought).
  • Published scores use bf16 weights; no source reports accuracy for the QAT Q4_0 GGUF, the LiteRT-LM GPU package, the MLX 4-bit conversion or the BaseRT Q4 bundle themselves.

Output reproducibility

Same model file, build, prompt and settings, repeated: 12 prompts × 3 repeats per process, fresh KV cache per request, stop tokens honoured, ≤128 tokens. Within process = repeats vs. the first repeat; across processes = a second fresh process with the same request sequence; across threads = a process with half the threads. Seeded = temperature 1.0, top-k 64, top-p 0.95, fixed seed; the seed control reruns with seed+1 and must change outputs, otherwise seeded reproducibility would be vacuous. Method: benchmark_methodology.md.

Key findings

  1. MLX has the lowest end-to-end latency on the headline workload (1,024 -> 256 tokens): 2.41 s, against 2.61 s for llama.cpp (Metal), 2.83 s for LiteRT-LM (ML Drift GPU) and 3.59 s for BaseRT. Relative to LiteRT-LM, decode throughput is 1.14x for MLX (118.5 vs 103.7 tok/s), 1.06x for llama.cpp (110.3) and 0.75x for BaseRT (77.6), all with tight 95% bootstrap intervals. These are reference configurations with different ~4-bit artifacts, not a matched-weight or tuned comparison.
  2. Prefill depends on input length, and the order of the frameworks changes with it. At 1,024 tokens (2 s idle before each request), MLX prefills at 4,002 tok/s, llama.cpp 3,413, BaseRT 3,369 and LiteRT-LM 2,752. LiteRT-LM is slowest on short prompts (551 tok/s at N = 128) but scales best. It passes llama.cpp from N = 4,096 and reaches 3,201 tok/s at N = 16,384, against 2,333 for llama.cpp. MLX prefills fastest from N = 1,024 upwards (4,303 tok/s at 16,384); llama.cpp is fastest at N <= 512.
  3. LiteRT-LM and BaseRT hold decode speed best as context grows. From N = 128 to 16,384 with 512-token decode, LiteRT-LM drops 5% (100.0 -> 94.8 tok/s) and BaseRT 5% (82.1 -> 77.9), against 19% for llama.cpp (116.5 -> 93.9) and 34% for MLX (126.8 -> 83.8). At 16,384 tokens, LiteRT-LM and llama.cpp decode fastest.
  4. Accuracy is equivalent across all four frameworks, so the speed comparison is valid. MMLU (2,000 items) is 78.4–79.5% and GSM8K (250 items) 93.6–94.0%. No paired difference is significant (McNemar p >= 0.06 for all 12 pairs). All four are reproducible per request, greedy and seeded, within and across processes and thread counts, and all use identical prompt token ids.
  5. Resource use differs more than speed. Host CPU time per request is 0.15 s for BaseRT, 0.59 s for LiteRT-LM, 0.59 s for llama.cpp and 1.87 s for MLX, which keeps 0.83 cores busy during decode. GPU memory above the pre-load baseline is 14.9 GB for llama.cpp and MLX, 15.2 GB for LiteRT-LM and 17.3 GB for BaseRT. Warm-cache load time is 0.8 s for BaseRT, 2.1 s for MLX, 2.6 s for llama.cpp and 8.3 s for LiteRT-LM.
  6. One LiteRT-LM process hit a GPU hang and silently returned invalid output. At N = 16,384 (sweep round 3), a LiteRT-LM command buffer caused a GPU hang (kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang). macOS restarted the GPU and ignored the process's further command buffers, but LiteRT-LM raised no error. It kept returning stale, slightly corrupted text with impossible timings (a 16,384-token prefill "in 12 ms" by its own counter). The harness now checks the macOS unified log after every native run. The process is excluded (that point has n = 10 instead of 15), not replaced. This was 1 of 30 LiteRT-LM GPU timing processes (its 9 accuracy and reproducibility processes were clean) and did not recur in 3 immediate reruns of the same point. No other process in the session, of any framework, logged a GPU error.
  7. TTFT depends on how long the GPU has been idle (see Caveats). After 0.5 s idle, LiteRT-LM prefills ~22% faster than in the headline. After 5 s, MLX prefill halves. Decode is unaffected.

Caveats

Scope and model equivalence

  • This is an open/reference comparison: each framework runs its own published ~4-bit artifact of Gemma 4 26B A4B with framework defaults. Quantization differs (LiteRT-LM GPU package: QAT, blockwise int4 weights, float activations; Google QAT Q4_0 GGUF; LM Studio QAT MLX: 4-bit g64 experts, 8-bit dense MLP and router; BaseRT catalog default-q4). No weight equivalence was established, so speed must be read together with the accuracy gate. The four configurations are not tuned "fastest" settings.
  • Prompt token ids are identical in every configuration (the hash in the Environment table). The prompt uses the 26B A4B chat template's non-thinking generation prompt, which ends with an empty thought channel (<|channel>thought\n<channel|>). The E2B suites don't use it, because the E2B template has no such block.

Environment and measurement

  • Native macOS 27.0.1 on the Apple M5 Max (40-core GPU, 64 GB unified memory, AC power, low-power mode off), not a VM. These results are not comparable with the Linux-VM CPU reports.
  • The machine and display were kept awake for the whole session (caffeinate -dims, plus the runner's own assertion), and pmset -g log shows no sleep or wake events in the run window. VS Code (which hosted the session) and the window server stayed open; mean system GPU utilization between requests was 6–10%, and GPU in-use memory before each model load was a stable ~0.81 GB.
  • GPU utilization is the system-wide IOAccelerator counter, used as an indicator only. It reads 99–100% at saturation and ~0% at idle, but overstates idle gaps shorter than ~1 s (a 25% duty cycle at 100 ms periods read as 51%). It is not per process, and there is no GPU power or energy figure: powermetrics needs root. CPU energy is the kernel's per-process CPU estimate and excludes GPU work.
  • Memory: compare frameworks on GPU in-use memory above the pre-load baseline (system-wide). phys_footprint includes MLX's Metal buffers but not llama.cpp's no-copy mmap'd weights, nor LiteRT-LM's or BaseRT's GPU weights, so footprint alone understates their memory use.
  • llama.cpp's driver timestamps tokens with CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW on macOS, the clock the monitor (Python 3.12 time.monotonic_ns) uses; libc++'s steady_clock there also counts sleep. Every request passed the clock-domain check.

Workload and framework behaviour

  • Headline: 1,024-token real-text prompt -> 256 greedy tokens (stop tokens ignored), context 4,096, 2 warm-up + 5 measured requests per process, 3 interleaved processes per configuration, 2 s idle between requests and 10 s between processes.
  • TTFT depends on how long the GPU idled before the request. In a separate idle-gap experiment (4 measured requests per point; runs labelled idlegap-*, not part of the headline), median prefill throughput in tok/s was:
Idle before requestlitert-lm/gpullama.cpp/metalmlx/metalbasert/metal
0.5 s3,3483,4454,2023,549
2 s (headline)2,6623,4203,9713,405
5 s2,6443,4101,9653,374

Decode throughput did not change. The headline uses 2 s, so it is neither the back-to-back best case nor the cold-GPU case.

  • Fixed-length decoding differs in mechanism, not work. llama.cpp and MLX feed a sampled stop token back, and LiteRT-LM uses its engine's num_decode_tokens. BaseRT stops on stop tokens internally and has no ignore-EOS option, so its driver counts the stop token and resumes with baseRT_generate_continue (eos_resumed in the raw data). A logit bias on the stop ids was rejected because it moved BaseRT off its fast decode path (77.6 -> 42–58 tok/s).
  • BaseRT streams in bursts. Tokens reach the caller in groups of about four (inter-token p50 ≈ 0.006 ms, p99 ≈ 52.5 ms). Decode throughput is unaffected, but TTFT is measured when the first token is available to the caller, which can be part of a burst. With the release's standard layout, the v0.4.0 engine logs get_pipeline: no function named 'moe_simd_gelu_gate_up_q4_sbf16'. Neither the standalone nor the embedded kernel library contains that kernel, and loading only the embedded copy gave the same speed and output.
  • Load times depend on the page cache. The four artifacts total ~62 GB on a 64 GB machine, so a model may have been partly evicted when its process started (e.g. one LiteRT-LM load took 48 s against ~8.2 s otherwise). LiteRT-LM GPU wrote no program cache to its --cache-dir.
  • MLX grows its KV cache on demand; the other engines allocate for the configured context (4,096 headline; 16,896 sweep).

Native-tool cross-check (same 1,024 / 256 shape)

Each framework's own benchmark tool, on the same model files (raw output under results/apple-m5-max/native-tools/). The harness rows are the headline medians.

ConfigNative toolTool prefill / decode (tok/s)Harness prefill / decode (tok/s)Explanation
litert-lm/gpulitert-lm benchmark --backend gpu -p 1024 -d 2561,219 / 107.42,752 / 103.7The tool creates a fresh engine per iteration, so each timed prefill is an engine's first prefill (~0.85 s; the harness's unmeasured first warm-up is ~0.88–0.94 s). Decode within 4%.
llama.cpp/metalllama-bench -ngl 999 -p 1024; -n 256 -d 10243,592 / 121.53,413 / 110.3Random token ids; excludes tokenization, and llama-bench does not copy the full 262k-entry logits to the host for an arg-max every token, which the driver does.
mlx/metalmlx_lm.benchmark -p 1024 -g 2564,585 / 119.54,002 / 118.5Back-to-back trials with no idle gap (cf. 4,202 tok/s at 0.5 s idle); random prompt tokens.
basert/metalbasert-bench -p 1024 -n 256 --tg-at 1024 --fill corpus:<harness passage>3,879 / 80.4 (92.1 from an empty context)3,369 / 77.6Back-to-back repetitions (cf. 3,549 tok/s at 0.5 s idle); decode is best-of-5, against the harness median; excludes tokenization.

Accuracy and output reproducibility

  • Accuracy uses the same deterministic 2,000-item MMLU subset and 250-item GSM8K subset as the earlier reports. Prompts are zero-shot, greedy and non-thinking, with MMLU answer-prefilled. Neither score is comparable with Google's published (thinking-mode, bf16) scores, which are for other benchmarks.
  • On ~3–5% of MMLU items, 26B A4B hedges ("not explicitly provided in the options …") within the 8-token answer budget. These are scored as wrong parse failures, not dropped, on identical items for every framework.
  • Accuracy and reproducibility runs overlapped with model downloads (network and disk only), as the methodology allows; timing runs did not. The recorded harness digest varies across runs because of report-rendering changes and driver fixes made during the session. Each framework's driver was unchanged across all of that framework's accuracy, reproducibility and timing processes: the MLX BOS fix and the BaseRT EOS-resume and config fixes came before any of those frameworks' recorded runs.

2. Building the native framework stack (pinned)

Metal runs on the macOS host, not in Docker. The setup script pins framework versions and verifies downloaded artifacts; BaseRT uses a prebuilt engine.

make native
make gpu-models

3. Machine setup & running the full benchmark suite

Use AC power with low-power mode off; keep other GPU clients idle. The suite prevents sleep and runs one benchmark process at a time.

make MACHINE=apple-m5-max SUITE=suites/gemma4-26b-a4b-gpu.json suite-perf
make MACHINE=apple-m5-max SUITE=suites/gemma4-26b-a4b-gpu.json suite-sequence
make MACHINE=apple-m5-max SUITE=suites/gemma4-26b-a4b-gpu.json suite-accuracy
make MACHINE=apple-m5-max SUITE=suites/gemma4-26b-a4b-gpu.json suite-repro
make MACHINE=apple-m5-max SUITE=suites/gemma4-26b-a4b-gpu.json native-report DATE=2026-10-22

4. Single-configuration performance commands

Each command uses the suite's workload, warm-ups, repetitions and interleaved round count for the selected configuration.

build/native/venv/bin/python scripts/suite.py perf --machine apple-m5-max --suite suites/gemma4-26b-a4b-gpu.json --only basert/metal
build/native/venv/bin/python scripts/suite.py perf --machine apple-m5-max --suite suites/gemma4-26b-a4b-gpu.json --only litert-lm/gpu
